summary: 路易·布莱叶幼年失明后发现，现有凸字书既笨重又难以书写。他把触觉信号改成可由一个指尖辨读的六点系统，并将其推广到音乐记谱。
logic: 学生用演奏证明实用性

paragraphs.brief: 1809年，路易斯·布莱尔出生在法国小村庄Coupvray.
sentences: Early Life and Blindness Louis Braille was born in 1809 in the small French village of Coupvray.
1809年，路易斯·布莱尔出生在法国小村庄Coupvray.
His father was a harness maker (a leather craftsman), and from a young age Louis liked to play in his father’s workshop.
他的父亲是一名制革工(皮革工匠)，从小路易就喜欢在父亲的车间里玩耍。
Tragically, at the age of three, Louis injured his eye with an awl (a sharp tool used for making holes in leather).
可悲的是，路易在三岁时用手电击(用来在皮革上打洞的锋利工具)打伤他的眼睛。
The wound became infected and the infection spread to his other eye, leaving him completely blind by age five.
伤口被感染，感染蔓延到他的另一只眼睛，5岁时他完全失明。
Growing up blind in the early 19th century was extremely challenging, but Louis’s parents were determined to help him lead a normal life.
19世纪初，盲人成长是极具挑战性的，但路易的父母决心帮助他过上正常的生活。
He proved to be a bright and creative child, and eventually earned a scholarship to attend the Royal Institute for Blind Youth in Paris.
他已证明是一个聪明和有创意的孩子，最终获得了奖学金，以便参加巴黎的皇家盲人青年研究所。
At that time, the few books available for blind readers had raised embossed print letters, which were bulky and difficult to read by touch.
当时，可供盲人阅读的少数书籍都印有大量印有印有纸，难以触读。
Louis was frustrated by how slowly he had to read under this system.
路易对他在这种制度下读得这么慢感到沮丧。
He dreamed of a better way for blind people to read and write independently.
他梦想着一个更好的方法盲人可以独立阅读和写作

paragraphs.brief: Louis B盲文作为该学院的学生，开始研究创造触觉写作的不同方法，即纸上可触摸读的提高标记系统。
sentences: Inventing the Braille System As a student at the Institute, Louis Braille began studying different ways of creating tactile writing – systems of raised marks on paper that could be read by touch.
Louis B盲文作为该学院的学生，开始研究创造触觉写作的不同方法，即纸上可触摸读的提高标记系统。
He learned of a code of raised dots and dashes devised by a French army captain for soldiers to share messages silently at night (this night writing inspired Louis greatly).
他了解到法国陆军上尉设计了一套 " 升起点 " 和 " 破折号 " 的守则，让士兵在夜间默默地分享信息(这一夜的写作极大地启发了路易)。
After years of experimentation, he finally developed a new system at age 15.
经过多年的实验他终于在15岁的时候开发了一套新的系统
Braille’s invention used a six-dot cell – six raised dots arranged in two columns of three – to represent letters and symbols.
盲文的发明用六点细胞 — — 六个点放在三列中的两列中 — — 来代表字母和符号。
By using different combinations of the six dots, he could create 63 possible patterns, each standing for a letter of the alphabet or a short word.
通过使用六点的不同组合，他可以创造63种可能的模式，每个模式都代表字母字母或一个简短的单词。
This six-dot tactile code was elegant in its simplicity: it was compact and could be read quickly with the fingertip.
这个六点触觉代码简洁而优雅：它很紧凑，可以用指尖快速阅读。
Louis Braille had essentially made it possible for blind people to read and write efficiently by touch, a revolutionary breakthrough.
路易盲文基本上使盲人能够通过触摸有效地阅读和写作，这是一个革命性的突破。
He even extended his dot system to cover musical notation, allowing blind students to read and write music as well.
他甚至将其点数系统扩大到包括音乐标记，使盲人学生也能够读写音乐。

paragraphs.brief: 一开始许多人认为路易的新点系统不会真正有效或实用。
sentences: Initial Skepticism and a Young Girl’s Tribute At first, many people did not believe that Louis’s new dot system would really work or be practical.
一开始许多人认为路易的新点系统不会真正有效或实用。

Sighted teachers at the Institute were accustomed to the old embossed-letter method and some feared that if blind students could read and write on their own, the sighted teachers might no longer be needed.
学院的有视力的教师习惯了旧的书写方法，有些人担心，如果盲人学生能够自己读写，那么眼中的教师就不再需要了。
Indeed, after an early director who supported Braille retired, a new school director even banned the use of Braille’s dot code for a time, worried that blind students were becoming “too independent”.
事实上，一个支持盲人文字的早期校长退休后，一个新的校长甚至暂时禁止使用盲人文字的点码，担心盲人学生会变得"过于独立".
Nevertheless, Braille’s students and friends continued to use his system in secret, convinced of its value.
然而，盲文学生和朋友仍然秘密地使用他的系统，相信它的价值。
A turning point came thanks to a public musical performance.
公共音乐表演带来了一个转折点。
One day, a young girl who had been blind since birth played the piano beautifully at a concert – delighting the audience.
有一天，一个从出生起就失明的年轻女孩在音乐会上演奏钢琴时非常漂亮，使观众欢欣鼓舞。
After the applause, the girl stood up and announced that everyone should thank Louis Braille, “who had made it possible for her to learn music and to play the piano.”
女孩在掌声后站起来，宣布每个人都应该感谢路易·布莱叶盲文，“她使她能够学习音乐和弹钢琴。”
Her ability to read music through Braille’s dot system had enabled her to become a skilled pianist.
她通过盲文点系统阅读音乐的能力，使她成为一名熟练的钢琴家。
This powerful testimony showed skeptics that Braille’s invention truly opened up opportunities for the blind.
盲文的发明真正为盲人开辟了机会。
The success of Braille’s system could no longer be denied.
盲文系统的成功再也不能否认了。

paragraphs.brief: 当路易的盲文朋友匆忙地告诉他女孩在移动的悼念时，他们发现他在床上生病 — — 盲文一直患上肺结核，而这个疾病很快会夺去他的生命。
sentences: Braille’s Reflections and Legacy When Louis Braille’s friends rushed to tell him about the girl’s moving tribute, they found him sick in bed – Braille had been suffering from tuberculosis, the illness that would soon claim his life.
当路易的盲文朋友匆忙地告诉他女孩在移动的悼念时，他们发现他在床上生病 — — 盲文一直患上肺结核，而这个疾病很快会夺去他的生命。
Upon hearing what happened at the concert, Louis was overcome with emotion and began to cry.
路易听到音乐会发生的事后情绪被克服开始哭泣
“This is the third time in my life that I have cried,” he told his friends.
“这是我一生中第三次哭泣，”他告诉他的朋友。
“The first time was when I became blind.
“第一次是当我失明的时候。
The second was when I first heard about ‘night writing.’
第二，当我第一次听到“夜写”的消息时。
And now I am crying because I know that my life has not been a failure.”
现在我哭是因为我知道我的生活并非失败。”
A few days later, Louis Braille died in Paris in 1852 at the age of 43.
几天后，路易斯的盲文于1852年在巴黎去世，43岁。
At the time of his passing, his writing system had still not been officially adopted by the authorities, and his death initially went almost unnoticed in the press.
在他去世时，他的书写系统仍未被当局正式采用，他的死亡最初在新闻界几乎无人注意。
However, Braille’s legacy would soon shine through.
但盲文的传承很快会闪耀出来。
Just two years after his death, the Braille dot system was finally endorsed at his former school in Paris and began to spread.
他去世仅两年后，盲文点系统终于被巴黎以前的学校认可，并开始扩散。

In 1878, an international congress on blind education officially recognized Braille’s code, and over the following decades it was gradually accepted worldwide as the standard method of reading and writing for the blind.
1878年，国际盲人教育大会正式认可盲文守则，并在随后几十年中逐渐被全世界接受为盲人阅读和写作的标准方法。

paragraphs.brief: 今天，全球有数百万盲人或视力障碍者使用盲文，该系统几乎被改写为每一种语言。
sentences: Today, millions of blind or visually impaired people around the globe use Braille, and the system has been adapted into nearly every language.
今天，全球有数百万盲人或视力障碍者使用盲文，该系统几乎被改写为每一种语言。

Over time, Braille’s code has seen various modifications and extensions – for example, special contractions were developed for faster reading, and new symbols were added for mathematics and scientific notation – but it still fundamentally relies on the six-dot matrix that Louis invented.
随着时间的推移，盲文的代码经历了各种修改和扩展 — — 例如，为更快的阅读开发了特殊的缩缩，为数学和科学符号添加了新的符号 — — 但基本上仍然依赖路易发明的六点矩阵。
In fact, Braille’s basic system remains “virtually unchanged to this day,” a testament to the brilliance of his design.
事实上，盲文的基本系统“基本上没有改变”，这证明了他的设计多么有才华。

Louis Braille’s innovation truly “opened the doors of knowledge to all those who cannot see,” and his six raised dots continue to empower blind individuals to read, write, and participate fully in literature, education, music, and everyday life.
路易·布莱叶的革新真正“打开了知识之门，让所有看不见的人都能看到 ”，他的六点发展继续赋予盲人阅读、写作和充分参与文学、教育、音乐和日常生活的能力。
